scope: BAS startup recovery of active rows orphaned shortly before restart

hypotheses.claim: An execution orphaned less than five minutes before startup survives the one-time recovery sweep indefinitely.
hypotheses.result: confirmed: a red regression with one-second-old RUNNING and PENDING rows recovered zero before the change

hypotheses.claim: A durable database heartbeat updates UpdatedAt and proves a fresh active row still has a live owner.
hypotheses.result: falsified by source inspection: executor heartbeats are timeline telemetry and do not update the execution row

hypotheses.claim: A periodic recovery sweep eventually handles active rows skipped at startup.
hypotheses.result: falsified by source inspection: the single production recovery call occurs before serving and has no periodic caller

root_cause.lifecycle_invariant: In the managed single-API lifecycle, startup recovery runs before the router and scheduler admit new work, so every persisted RUNNING or PENDING row belongs to the previous process. UpdatedAt is not an ownership signal.

changes.implementation: Renamed startup recovery to RecoverInterruptedExecutions and now queries all RUNNING and PENDING rows separately with unbounded status-filtered queries; every returned row is marked interrupted before requests are served, without an age threshold.
changes.simplification: Removed the five-minute threshold, its configurable option, and unused per-execution result detail fields. Recovery results now retain only active, recovered, and failed counts consumed by the startup caller.
regressions: One-second-old RUNNING and PENDING rows must both be interrupted at startup.
1,000 newer completed rows do not hide older active rows; the same test confirms a one-minute-old active row is also interrupted.
